Its entry calls the Warring States forms phonosemantic, from 木 with 不 supplying sound, and says a horizontal stroke over 不 and short strokes in one graph are decorative. The entry describes variation in Han forms and cites vessel uses, the measure phrase 一杯水 in Mencius, and other examples. These are the book’s claims and citations; they do not establish dates of the cited physical witnesses or a full semantic chronology.
